skeleton:
Oven-Tray Full English Breakfast

British · Easy · Serves 4

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The full English solved for a crowd: one large roasting tray, one hot oven, everything cooked in place and landing together. This is the technique behind every good hotel breakfast tray and every smart B&B's "help yourself" — components arranged in zones, staggered onto the tray in the order they cook, the whole breakfast emerging at the single moment the eggs are ready. For four people it halves the washing-up; for six (see the big-batch master) it is the only sane method. The tray's advantage over the pan is even, all-around heat: bacon stays flat instead of curling, sausages brown on every side without turning, mushrooms and tomatoes roast in their own juices rather than stewing. Its one weakness is the same — no direct fat contact means no pan-fried crust — so the eggs and fried bread are finished in a pan for the last five minutes, borrowing the tray's rendered bacon fat. The oven does the volume; the pan does the sparkle.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The meats

The vegetables

The potato and bread

The eggs

Seasoning and fat

- **Tray choice matters:** a heavy roasting tray at least 30 × 40 cm, NOT non-stick if you can help it — the bacon fond that sticks is the flavour base for the eggs' pan. Line nothing; parchment steams the underside of everything. - **Preheat the tray.** A cold tray into a hot oven wastes the first ten minutes; a preheated one sears on contact. Put the empty tray in as the oven climbs to 220 °C (fan 200 °C). - **Par-boil and cool the potatoes** if starting from raw — 8 minutes in boiling salted water, drained, steamed dry, cooled. Cold par-boiled wedges roast to crisp outsides and fluffy insides; raw wedges will not catch up. - **Plan the staging:** the recipe runs in three arrivals onto the tray — potatoes and onions first (longest), sausages and mushrooms second, bacon, black pudding and tomatoes last. Count backwards from the eggs' final 5 minutes.

Doneness & Quality Checkpoints

  • Potatoes: 25 minutes to deep golden, crisp-edged, fluffy within.
  • Sausages: +12 minutes, browned all over, once-pricked, juices clear.
  • Bacon/pudding/tomatoes: +10 minutes — flat glassy bacon, crusted pudding, jammy tomatoes.
  • Eggs: pan-fried in the tray's bacon fat, whites set, yolks running; all zones landing simultaneously.

Oven-Tray Full English Breakfast

Prep: 15 minutes · Cook: 40 minutes · Total: 55 minutes · Serves 4

Ingredients

The meats

  • 8 rashers (400 g) smoked back bacon
  • 8 pork sausages (about 640 g), pricked once each
  • 8 thick slices (400 g) black pudding

The vegetables

  • 4 medium vine tomatoes (400 g), halved through the equator
  • 300 g chestnut mushrooms, left whole if small
  • 2 red onions (300 g), cut into thick wedges

The potato and bread

  • 600 g potatoes, par-boiled 8 minutes, cooled and cut into thick wedges — or 4 frozen hash browns (360 g)
  • 8 slices (400 g) thick white bread, for fried bread (pan stage)

The eggs

  • 8 large eggs (440 g)
  • 30 g butter, for the egg pan

Seasoning and fat

  • 30 ml / 28 g olive oil
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 2 g black pepper
  • 1 tsp (3 g) brown sugar, for the tomatoes
  • 5 g fresh thyme leaves
  • Brown breakfast sauce and tomato ketchup, to serve

Instructions

  1. **First arrival — potatoes and onions, 25 minutes.** Pull the hot tray, add the oil, and turn the potato wedges and onion wedges through it with half the salt and pepper and half the thyme. Return to the oven, shelf one below centre, and roast 25 minutes, turning once at 15 minutes. Checkpoint — at 25 minutes the wedges are deeply golden on their cut faces with crisp edges and fluffy interiors, the onions have charred sweet at their tips and softened to slivers, and the tray carries a film of golden fat and fond.
  2. **Second arrival — sausages and mushrooms, plus 12 minutes.** Push the potatoes to one half of the tray. Add the sausages (pricked once) and the mushrooms, tossing the mushrooms in the tray's fat. Roast another 12 minutes, turning the sausages once at 6 minutes. Checkpoint — the sausages are evenly browned all over with taut skins and clear juices when nicked; the mushrooms have browned and glossed, shrunk by a third, no grey watery pooling.
  3. **Third arrival — bacon, black pudding, tomatoes, plus 10 minutes.** Lay the bacon rashers over any free surface, the black pudding slices beside, and the tomato halves cut-face up in a corner, each sprinkled with sugar, salt, and a drop of the tray's fat. Roast the final 10 minutes. About halfway through this stage, put the egg pan and a second small pan for the bread on the hob over low heat to warm gently. Checkpoint — the bacon has rendered flat, its fat glassy and amber-edged; the black pudding is crusted dark on both faces, holding firm; the tomatoes have slumped, jammy, their cavities reduced to a bubbling glaze. Everything else has deepened another shade. The whole tray smells like the outside of a good café.
  4. **The pan stage — eggs and fried bread, 5 minutes.** Tilt the tray, spoon off 2–3 tablespoons of the rendered bacon fat into the warmed egg pan, and raise it to medium. Crack in the eggs, 4 at a time if the pan is 24 cm, and fry to the butter-basted master's spec, basting with the hot fat — 2–3 minutes for set whites and running yolks. Meanwhile fry the bread in the second pan in a knob of the butter (or the remaining tray fat) until golden, about 1 minute per side. Checkpoint — whites fully set, yolks liquid, edges lacy-gold; the bread is crisp-edged and grease-free on the rack for 10 seconds before plating.
  5. **Landing — everything at once.** Bring the tray to the table on a board, or plate in the kitchen: bacon, sausage, black pudding, potato wedge or two, mushrooms, onion, tomato, fried bread, and the egg crowning it. Sauce dishes alongside. Checkpoint — the synchronous plate: every zone hot, the bacon still crackling as it's served, the yolk breaking on command over the bread. Four plates from one tray, five minutes of pan.

Finish & Plate

Serve the tray itself at the table — café-plated individually, or family-style with the tray on a trivet and everyone serving clockwise from the eggs. The roasted onions are this version's signature — sweet, charred-tipped, unexpected — and earn their place permanently. Builder's tea, brown sauce, tomato ketchup for the potato wedges.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Everything steamed pale, nothing brownedTray crowded, lined with parchment, or oven runs cool30 × 40 cm minimum, unlined, preheated; verify 220 °C
Potatoes raw in the middleAdded raw, not par-boiledThe 8-minute par-boil is not optional
Black pudding crumbledSliced thin or stayed past 10 minutes1.5 cm slices; it leaves with the bacon
Bacon pale and flabbyAdded too earlyIt belongs to the final 10 minutes only
Eggs overcooked by platingCooked before the tray was outEggs start when the tray stops — reverse order fails

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **Make-ahead:** the tray's meats and vegetables reheat superbly — 180 °C for 10 minutes on the same tray. Cooked tray components keep 3 days refrigerated; eggs are always fresh. - **Variation — vegetarian tray:** swap the meats for vegetarian sausages (add with the mushrooms stage), haloumi slabs (final 10 minutes), and extra portobello caps; the zones and timing hold unchanged. - **Variation — the honey-mustard glaze:** brush the sausages with 15 g honey mixed with 5 g wholegrain mustard when they go in; a weekend flourish that nobody protests. - **Scaling:** the tray method doubles to six servings on a larger tray with the same three stages — the big-batch master covers the full choreography.
